ledger.note: Searched the Federal Register notice for FERC docket CP15-14 and the EIA entry for the Southern Indiana Market Project. They describe a lateral serving two industrial customers in Posey County, Indiana. No source ties it to LNG exports or an LNG terminal.
Read the EIA entry for the West Greenville-Elkton Lateral. It is an expansion serving Kentucky gas demand with no LNG mention. Searched for an LNG tie and found none.
Read the EIA entry and a Federal Register notice for the Western Kentucky Lateral (docket CP15-105). It serves a TVA power plant at Paradise Fossil. No source ties it to LNG.

Searched for the Texas Independence Pipeline and LNG. Sources describe it as an Energy Transfer intrastate gas line, with no LNG tie. The only LNG project found is Lake Charles LNG in Louisiana, and nothing connects this line to it.
Searched for the ET Carthage Loop Expansion and LNG. Sources describe an Energy Transfer intrastate expansion with no LNG tie. The LNG-linked Carthage projects found belong to other companies.

Searched for the Enterprise Texas Intrastate System and LNG feedgas. Sources say the system serves Corpus Christi and Houston Ship Channel markets, and that Enterprise planned export-oriented upgrades. No source names this system as delivering gas to an LNG terminal or ties it to LNG exports.
Read the EIA entry and the listed references for the Tioga to Emerson Pipeline. It is a shelved takeaway line from the Bakken to Minnesota. No LNG tie appears in any source.
Searched for the Trailblazer Pipeline and LNG. Sources describe a line now carrying carbon dioxide between Wyoming and Nebraska or Iowa, with no LNG tie.
Read the EIA entries and the listed references for the Dakota Natural Gas and Traill County pipelines. They serve North Dakota local distribution customers. No LNG tie appears.

Searched for the Trans-Alaska gas line segment from Pump Station 1 to Pump Station 4 and LNG. The segment supports the North Slope oil pipeline system. Alaska LNG planning sources describe a separate 807-mile line to a Nikiski plant, and nothing ties this segment to that project.

Searched for the Trans-Union Interstate Pipeline and LNG. Sources describe a late-1990s line to an Arkansas power plant, with no LNG tie. The Federal Register notice from 2000 also names no LNG customer.
Read the EIA entries and the listed references for TransColorado. They describe a gas line from the San Juan Basin to Colorado and New Mexico with no LNG tie.

Searched for the Transco 85 North Expansion and LNG. Station 85 receives LNG regasified at import terminals, but no source ties this expansion itself to LNG exports. The Federal Register notice for docket CP09-57 describes a power-plant supply expansion.
Searched for the Transco Dalton Expansion and LNG feedgas. Sources describe a lateral serving Georgia power generation and gas utilities, with no LNG tie.
Searched for the Transco Diamond East Project and LNG. Sources describe a Pennsylvania to New Jersey expansion that was later put on hold or assumed cancelled. No LNG tie appears.

Searched for the Hillabee Expansion Phase 1 and LNG. Sources describe a Transco expansion feeding Florida power generators through Sabal Trail. Any LNG link is only indirect, through the Transco system in general, so nothing ties this phase to an LNG export.
Searched for the Hillabee Expansion Phase 2 and LNG. Sources describe the same Florida power supply expansion as Phase 1. No source ties this phase to LNG exports.
Searched for the Hillabee Expansion Phase 3 and LNG. The EIA entry says the phase is on hold and supplies Sabal Trail. No source ties it to LNG exports.
Read the EIA entry and the Federal Register notice for the Transco Leidy East Expansion. It serves Northeast distribution markets. Searched for an LNG tie and found none.

Searched for the Transco Leidy Southeast Expansion and LNG. Sources describe a Pennsylvania to New Jersey expansion for distribution and power demand. The only Cove Point mention concerns a different, earlier Transco project.
